title: How a calculator becomes a gaming PC
lines: Your calculator does math. Congratulations, you've built a computer.
But it adds two numbers at a time, and you want to play games.
So you pack billions of tiny switches onto one chip that does math billions of times a second. This is the CPU.
But a chip alone does nothing, so you plug it into a board covered in tiny copper roads. This is the motherboard.
But the CPU keeps waiting on your slow files.
So you give it a desk right next to it, for whatever it's working on. This is the RAM.
But the second you switch it off, the desk is wiped clean.
So you add a drive that remembers everything, even with the power off. This is the SSD.
But now the CPU is hot enough to fry an egg.
So you bolt on metal fins and a fan. This is the cooler.
But a game is millions of pixels, sixty times a second, and your CPU is drawing a slideshow.
So you add a card with thousands of tiny cores, each drawing a few pixels at once. This is the GPU.
Now it's so hungry, your lights flicker every time you open a game.
So you add a box that turns wall power into something it can eat. This is the power supply.
Put it in a glass case, with rainbow lights that do absolutely nothing. Congratulations, you've built a gaming PC.
